description: Thin roots bound in twine and dried past bending. Sold in autumn, to go into the ground in spring.
lore: A woman on the north road digs, trims, ties and dries them, forty bundles a season, and sells them off a board at the autumn markets to anyone with a bed to fill. Most of it is trade. One order is not.

The same order every year, placed in advance, in the same hand: white bellflower, two bundles, held back until the frost breaks. [[characters/cfe826c1|Jehanne]] has never said whether they took. The digger has never asked, and has settled it privately, and will tell you so over a cup — that the ground behind that chapel must be a sight by now, white to the wall, thick as a hedge, coming again every spring for eleven years. She has not gone to look. She has eleven years of the same order in her book in the same hand, which she says is a better thing to own than a garden.
gm_notes: The digger is wrong and will never find out; anyone who has read the Thornstag record knows what happens to that bed each autumn. Jehanne reorders anyway. Do not let the digger meet the stag.
